To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of tamoxifen and raloxifene in the context of an established national breast screening programme is feasible, safe and acceptable to women.

the risk of breast cancer can be reduced by 40–50% in women with a family history of breast cancer, by 60–75% in women with BRCA1/BRCA2 mutations, by 50% in women at risk of developing breast cancer because of their lifestyle and by 30% in women with an increased risk of breast cancer because of a previous history of benign breast disease.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the prevention of breast cancer, and in particular the role of tamoxifen, a selective oestrogen receptor modulator.

the development of a new approach for the prevention of breast cancer, using the national breast screening programme to identify women at increased risk of breast cancer and then offer them interventions to reduce that risk.
the identification of women at high risk of breast cancer and the prevention of breast cancer in these women.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence for the efficacy of breast cancer prevention in the form of tamoxifen is weak.

the use of tamoxifen in women at high risk of developing breast cancer is effective at reducing the risk of breast cancer and the use of tamixifen in women at average risk of developing breastcancer is not effective.

the current evidence does not support the widespread use of tamoxifen or raloxifene for the prevention of breast cancer in asymptomatic women, but the use of these drugs in high-risk groups is justified, and the benefits of such use outweigh the risks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
breast cancer is a preventable disease.
the results of the IBIS-I and -II trials, and other data from the IBIS group, show that anastrozole has the potential to reduce the risk of breast cancer in women at increased risk of the disease.
breast cancer is preventable in the context of breast screening.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the risk of breast cancer is not static and can be modified by a number of lifestyle and environmental factors.
we have a very effective way to prevent breast cancer in the UK.
we can prevent breast cancer in women who have a family history of the disease.
